summary: Tested new WhatsApp Business and Blockchain Credentials (Sepolia) modules. Backend: 22/23 pytest passed (96%). Frontend: HR-side Blockchain Credentials page fully working — page loads with Sepolia badge, Connected status, correct wallet 0xb5aB...42Ff39, 0.000000 ETH (Low), faucet links, list with Verify/Anchor/Revoke buttons. Issue New flow creates credential successfully (UI Test Credential appeared in list). Verify flow shows green 'Valid Credential' panel with recovered signer matching expected issuer. Anchor buttons correctly disabled (balance < 0.001 ETH). Revoke shows 'Revoked' badge. WhatsApp webhook verify, receive, send (HR), 401/403 role gates, and /messages all correct. Send-to-Meta returns 200 with status='send_failed' as expected (not 500). Anchor returns 400 'Insufficient Sepolia balance' as expected. Master password regression passes.

minor.issue: When an unknown WhatsApp number sends a message, the bot tries to notify the sender via send_wa_message (which fails because Meta rejects non-allow-listed numbers). The exception bubbles to the outer try/except returning {status:'error', detail:'...'} instead of the documented {status:'unknown_user'}. The HTTP status is still 200, so Meta won't retry. Fix: wrap the unknown-user notification send in its own try/except so the function always returns 'unknown_user'.

rca_of_the_issue: Unknown-user webhook returning status:'error' instead of 'unknown_user' — root cause: send_wa_message('❌ Your number is not registered...') at /app/backend/routes/whatsapp_routes.py line ~318 raises httpx.HTTPStatusError (Meta returns 400 for non-allow-listed numbers); this exception escapes to the outer try/except at line 365-367 which returns {status:'error'}. Mitigation: wrap that single send call in try/except so the function unconditionally returns JSONResponse(200, {status:'unknown_user'}).
